ROSELAND, N.J., Sept. 2, 2026 / PRNewswire/ -- Private-sector employment increased by 38,000 jobs in August, according to the ADP National Employment Report® produced by ADP Research in collaboration with the Stanford Digital Economy Lab ("Stanford Lab"). 

For all private-sector workers in the United States, base pay rose 3.2% and gross pay was up 4.7% year over year, according to ADP Pay Insights.

Base pay for job-stayers rose 3.0% year-over-year; base pay for job-changers increased 4.7%.

Gross pay for job-stayers rose 4.4% year-over year; gross pay for job-changers increased 7.3%.

BLS Jobs Revision Shows Smaller Employment Growth Loss – CEPR

#### Jobs Revisions Show Small Loss, Manufacturing Among Big Losers

Aug 31, 2026

By Dean Baker

#### On This Page

The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) released preliminary numbers for its annual benchmark revisions to job growth on Friday. After two years of very large downward revisions, the preliminary number for the year from March 2025 to March 2026 was a minus 79,000 jobs. This follows a downward revision of 898,000 in the year to March of 2025, and a downward revision of 598,000 in the year to March of 2024. 

The smaller revision makes it less newsworthy than would be the case with a larger revision, but there are still a few points worth noting:

1. The smaller revision could be due in part to less immigration;
2. The drop in manufacturing makes the fall in jobs in the sector even larger;
3. Retail also had a large drop, although construction employment was revised up.

1. What Is a Benchmark Revision?

The data in the monthly jobs report (usually released in the 1st Friday of the month) is based on two surveys, the Current Population Survey (CPS or “household survey”) and the Current Employment Statistics (CES or “establishment survey”). The establishment survey data in the report is subject to an annual revision exercise that includes a benchmark revision. 1 2
